newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end mostly down amid caution.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end mostly down amid caution.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended mostly down on Thursday and a cautious mood prevailed on the markets as most listed companies had yet to issue their interim results, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index, the only rising index, closed up 0.477 points, or 0.64 percent, to 74.999 points on volume of 14.739 million shares worth $5.002 million.
The Shenzhen B index fell 0.75 points, or 0.56 percent, to 132.58 points on thin turnover of HK$34 million.

The Shanghai A index fell 26.691 points, or 2.13 percent, to 1,227.928 on volume of 310.212 million shares worth 3.780 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index lost 79.529 points or 2.08 percent to 3,741.811 points.
The Shenzhen domestic A share index shed 10.79 points, or 2.56 percent, to 410.42 points with turnover shrinking to 5.2 billion yuan from 7.7 billion yuan on Wednesday.
"No one is trading actively," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "Investors don't want to risk their money because no clear market trend has emerged."
Interim results, which companies were required to report before the end of August, might help provide some direction to the market, brokers said.

Some foreign investors were looking towards a major Communist Party meeting in September or October, which would chart China's future development, to provide fresh direction to the market, brokers said.
"There won't be much news, positive or negative, before October," said an analyst.
Brokers also said the B share market's performance would largely depend on A shares.
"B shares can not do well if A shares stagnate," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Brokers said sharp declines in market giant Shenzhen Development Bank exacerbated the A share retreat.
The bank's shares tumbled 2.04 yuan to 34.93 yuan, driven down by disappointment over the company's 1997 earnings prospects, brokers said.
Volume reached 17 million shares, making the bank the most actively traded Shenzhen A share.

Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co was the most actively traded Shanghai B share on institutional cross-trading amid mixed views about the company's prospects. It ended up $0.014 or 3.48 percent to $0.416 on volume of around 3.3 million shares.
Conglomerate China Vanke was the poorest performer among Shenzhen B shares, falling HK$0.44 or 7.69 percent to HK$5.28.
Chemical fibre maker Searainbow Group, which was suspended from trading on Thursday morning, opened the afternoon session at its 10 percent limit-down at 8.74 yuan and stayed there towards the close.
The Bank of China on Thursday announced that it would sue Searainbow if it continued to delay repayment of a loan amounting to nearly US$16 million in balance and interest.
Searainbow said it was unable to repay the debt on time due to a bad investment and was trying to settle the issue.
